title: The AI Pivot: With Chris White of Prefect & Bryan Bischof of Hex
talk_summary: A panel with Chris White (Prefect) and Bryan Bischof (Hex) about how two data-tooling startups integrated AI into their products, covering build-vs-buy, evals, failure modes, and rollout. The most transferable content is about evaluation discipline (binary evals, typed outputs, prod-close evals) and designing for failure modes/observability rather than chat interfaces.

takeaways.technique: Binary yes/no evals instead of latent/similarity metrics
takeaways.what_they_do: They boil each task down to a clear human-meaningful binary judgment and run evals on that, explicitly rejecting BLEU-style similarity and KL-divergence approaches for LLM outputs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: boil it down to Binary yes or Nos and run your evals

takeaways.technique: Evals as close to production as possible, built in-house
takeaways.what_they_do: They chose to build their own eval harness rather than buy, because evals need deep hooks into the actual platform and should run against prod-like conditions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: eval should be as closest to production as possible is literally like using prod when possible

takeaways.what_they_do: They push LLM outputs toward guaranteed typed outputs (function calling / schema-typed returns) so downstream code and tests can assert on shape, making testing trivial compared to free-string prompts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: bringing it into the back end is just like having these typed handshakes

takeaways.technique: Design around failure modes and observability first
takeaways.what_they_do: When asked what agent builders should know, they said to think about failure modes up front: runaway processes, odd inputs/outputs, and an observability/debug layer wired in early.
takeaways.evidence_quote: think about failure modes I think that is the biggest thing so like runaway process CES

takeaways.what_they_do: They flag caching as essential for LLM workflows but also 'the root of all evil', implying it must be scoped carefully to avoid stale/incorrect reuse.
takeaways.evidence_quote: caching is like is the only time I will ever say this is definitely your friend in some of these situations uh but is also the root of all evil

takeaways.what_they_do: Hex keeps a roadmap sized for 20 engineers staffed by ~5, deliberately staying slim and prioritizing hard; Prefect similarly scoped AI work to marginal, narrow wins rather than arbitrary codegen.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I have a road map long enough for 20 engineers and we continue to stay around five
